reasoning: Hashes, spans and inline quotations all check out, the inventory (one suspension sentence) is complete, and the substantive analysis is sound: EO 12553 revokes the order by number, with no effective-date or savings wording, and the National Emergencies Act exclusion and the DOPMA repeal of 10 U.S.C. 6372 and 6386 effective 1981-09-15 are accurately disclosed as unnamed earlier candidates under the 2026-10-21 option C ruling. The claim nevertheless records the first end and whole-order end as 1983-02-25, three years before EO 12553 was signed (1986-02-25). That date matches no source, and it contradicts the claim's own mechanism text, judgment_reason, source signing_date and the OFR catalog. A wrong end date in the gated date fields requires rejection even though the actor and mechanism are right. Secondary observations, not grounds on their own: (1) my Cruden by-number run returns only EO 11436 itself; EO 12553's table lists '11436' without an 'Executive Order' prefix, so the scan does not reproduce the statement that it 'finds no held later order citing this order other than copies of EO 12553' (the producer's LOOKUPS output was not opened under blinding); (2) the rationale says the page 17943 was not confirmed from the extracted text while claim_kit records original_pages_confirmed true; the OFR catalog citation does supply 33 FR 17943. Corrected dates would be 1986-02-25 in both fields.
